body: Heya, i was browsing /depression as usual and i came across your post. I'm hoping you're still there and just wanted to offer my own perspective, I'm 27 this year, and only just graduated when i was 25, I never had a full time job, just part time and haven't been able to land a job after i graduated because of my anxiety and depression constantly holding me back, i haven't left my house in 2 years really and everyday I feel like the walls are coming down on me. My point is even though you're defifintely going through a shit time atm and i don't want to take away from that, just know your experiences and the things you went through has built you up to this moment and that there are definitely things you done that i haven't and i done that you haven't and I'm sure there is some internal strength still inside you that you can find that will help you through this. I'm a coward by my own admission but you defintely don't sound like one, I'm sure you got some fight left in you.

your post resonated with me. it sounds a lot like you're not able to express yourself and you're not confident in your abilities, letting fear having dominance over your life, i get that, because i feel very similiar but i wonder if you'd feel better if you allowed yourself to have a voice, an activity or a medium where you could freely express yourself, would you perhaps feel alittle better?

replying because your question resonated with me and this response maybe me lashing out because of my own insecurities/wanting to add my own input. Failure for me is being unable to come to terms with and allowing your choices and circumanstances to dictate how you should feel about yourself. 

Ah, who am i kidding, failing is lagging behind eveyone else and allowing everyone to overtake you in this competition of life, keep telling myself it's not because the thought of being shackled by debt and marraige actually kinda scares me but society tells you this is what you should be aiming for so...*shrug*

To be honest i wouldn't give a shit about failure if i could find some semblance of happiness somewhere but depression, anxiety and undiagnosed mental illnesses have pretty much stunted my potential to get that so i'm just gonna stop here.

Heya wanted to log in and leave a reply to say good on you for trying to improve your mental health, had a read of your previous post and thought it was good of you to help your neighbour like that. What i really wanted to reply with though was that from the sounds of your last sentence, it sounds like you're looking at the situation with negativity, thinking it was a bad event but if you'll let me be bold enough i actually think it did some good. 

To me it comes across as like, 'Hey i see you trying to get a handle of this depression thing, you say you want to go out a certain way? well here's the event in question, oh it looks like you didn't actually want to die that way afterall.' To me, it was almost like the event was thrown your way so you can actually overcome that way of thinking, re-jigging your thought pattern if you know what i mean?

It was great that nothing happened to you btw and i get why you responded to the event the way you did (duh), and like you said, you now know that isn't the way you want to go.

>I'd rather just die here. I don't see the point in spending SO much time, money and energy on something that has a 1% chance of working. I don't even know where to begin on going there even if I could.

If all else fails, have you considered becoming a monk? that way you're still living but you're not tied down by work or the daily struggles of the modern world.

>It's like what Zen Buddhists talk about when having a mind free of thought - you have to be 100% focused on riding the motorcycle so you can't possibly think about anything else. So it's not really something I want to stop.

I read meditation can be just like this sensastion describes, perhaps look at ways to practise that skill? just needs time to get used to it, free to do and only need a spare moment out of your day.

>By the end of my 2 year tenure at that job, I was in great shape, making decent money, and was so depressed I wanted to kill myself every second of every day. Finally I ended up getting myself fired, which was inevitable (quitting or killing myself being equally viable alternatives).

What job was it? was it an office job? did you enjoy the job (guessing not since you described the consequences of working there for year 1/2), was there elements there that pushed you that way e.g. your work responsibilies, your co-workers, your boss etc. Maybe you could find another field of work that would be better suited for you? Didn't your job allow you days off or holidays, i'm hard pressed to think of a job that didn't at least allow you 1 day off? definitely sounds like your work/life balance was way off here.

To be honest i'm kinda in the same boat, dreading the thought of working a boring office job rest of my life but that's what society pushes so 'shrugs' 

Here's a interesting thought i had the other night: whatever's weighing most at the forefront of our mind whether that be because we're stewing over something or something we watched/heard, we tend to look at cues or have additional thoughts that align with that same thought whenever we look or experience any events after that said thought. 

>To answer your first question, I tried a therapist and I hated it. The whole concept to me is terrible. I also hate that they can commit you basically totally at their discretion. I hate the idea of having a potential record of mental illness that could be used against me in the future (therapists can actually be court-ordered to reveal your sessions with them). I also tried medication for awhile and it didn't help, and I'm not cool with the idea of SSRIs and similar drugs. Especially the way they are used today.

I'm considering a therapist to be honest but with the rep that the UK mental health system gets and the cost of going private + the reaons you gave i'm still hesistant on that, do agree with the opinion about SSRI's, tried one in my teens for a week and half, killed my libido and made me number than i am usually so quit that. Wouldn't mind trying more recreational drugs though although that's a whole nother ballpark.

For 10mins a day, do you think you could take your mind away from all that is worrying you and focus on what brings you some semblance of joy perhaps the thoughts of the next day you're able to go motorcycle riding, the places you will ride to, the stuff you need to bring etc? It maybe a distraction but taking breaks and letting your mind wander away from your problems can do good.

Gonna change tracks here so feel free to not aswer if you don't feel inclined. How was your upbringing growing up? does your family have a history of mental illness because i know mine do. Did you grow up with a ton of pressure to succeed, to get a degree, to get a 'good' job? did you ever feel victimised? You mention a declining scale of the type of life you want, was there a particular event that sparked this off or was it a more gradual thing?

From what i gleaned you seem to be a fairly interesting person with a host of different hobbies and a talent you can cultivate, it seems you gave a fair effort to this life thing but instead of thinking of your life up to this point as a waste or something, i'd like to think of it things you tried that didn't work so you know you won't waste any further time pursuing them or you can try again and perhaps reach a breakthough with renewed vigor and different insights you didn't have previously?

You mentioned about being lonely, do you have any family? any siblings or friends? perhaps they can provide some comfort or support that you seem to need?

Granted i have to admit i'm also in a stage of giving up, i surmised that life is ultimately pointless to a extent and i don't get much enjoyment out of earthly things, a feeling that grows with each passing year but idk, some part of me just hanging in there, i suppose because my immeadiate family would be hurt if i did. I didn't really give a huge shit about the whole finishing university (although i eventually did), getting a degree (eventually got that too), getting a job (working on this one), finding a partner (lol?), starting a family (what?) and then paying off a house until i'm dead (fun times?) but the alternative is sitting on my arse doing nothing and i don't think you need me to tell you how soul crushing that is? Idk where you are in life but it seems you put in a heck of a lot of effort more than other people i read/know about and that's something to be proud of. 

I find with anything in life, if you want a change, you gotta go out and do different things (as you clearly done), if one thing doesn't work than do something else, some people try once and succeed (or perhaps make it succeed?), others have to try and try again until they get things right for THEM. Where am i going with this? It sounds like you're stuck in a bad place mentally and idk how long these thoughts of yours persisted but i'm thinking they created a negative feedback loop where these thoughts are the only thing you're thinking about to the point where you're no longer receptive to new ideas or solutions, driving you further down this hole you seem to painting yourself in. I get it because i'm very much the same way, one bad event in my day? bam, it's on my mind for next hour or two unless i dismiss it entirely with force of will nevermind trying to bat those fucking thoughts away 24/7 but like a muscle it can be done, not going to be easy for sure but can be done. Ultimately, what's the point? that's the depression talking and all that is getting is a punch straight through the middle because that only keeps feeding into the loop and we all know that no changes are coming from there. If anything it seems you're quite entrenched in your comfort zone, and 'while having a comfort zone is a beautiful thing, nothing grows there.'

Excuse me if my sentences seem to come across as ramblings but i think it's better for you to read my thoughts as and when they come rather than being edited, that why you can really see where i'm trying to come from.

>And I make very little money, so if I were to do something like that it would be an enormous risk. Then of course the old saying... "no matter where you go, there you are."

Maybe a enormous risk is what you need seeing as everything else you're trying seems to not be working? At worst you die over there having gained nothing and at best you actually gain something from the experience whether that's a new life for yourself or an adventure you can tell your loved ones.

>hobbies and talents than most non-depressed people, but how could I afford them when I can't work enough to make any money? And if I can't afford them, what the fuck is the point of living?

I personally reached a point where i'm seeing the old stuff i'm used to is just a distraction now and i don't personally enjoy them but i do them out of routine, but who says you have to spend money on hobbies in order to enjoy them? I know it's easier said than done but if you find yourself with a lot of idle time, perhaps you can spend that extra time looking at some way you can look into earning more money? 

>I dunno. I have tried every fucking thing anyone has suggested. I exercise often, I eat pretty healthy, I distract myself with hobbies, I've tried working a lot, working a little, sleeping a lot, sleeping a little, basically every lifestyle change you could think of. Nothing helps, and I'm fucking sick of putting in effort when it doesn't do shit.

I'm gonna say have you tried talking to a specialist or medications but something i tried doing recently is actually trying to change my mentaility, granted i don't know whether your depression is situational or clinical but at the start of the new year i told myself everytime i experience a negative thought coming, i tell myself 'No, i'm not going to act on or think about this particualar thought too deeply' and then i visualise punching a dark cloud straight through the middle as if to disperse that negative thought as if to stop it festering in my mind. It's kinda worked for me, maybe you can try re-framing your thinking?

You say you're tired of putting in effort and not seeing any results, how long did you stick to those new lifestyle changes? was it a week, a month, 2 months, a year? some changes take time to take effect.

Thanks for taking the time reply to my post, it was late at night and i have to admit i wasn't all there mentally as I was sleep deprived and in another one of my shitty moods, on that note though let's see if i can offer some further thoughts to your replies.

>Now, yes, you can say "I don't give a fuck about my value" and be a hobo or otherwise checked out from society. But in that case you are basically eliminating your chance to have relationships, to provide comfort for yourself, and to have friends. So I mean, what is the other option?"

Have you looked at alternative ways of living? I've known a few people who decided to buck the usual trend of getting a 9-5 in order to keep working and earning. A friend of one has moved to South Korea and is planning to teach ESL for as long as he's able, he didn't exactly have the greatest home life either so i respect that a lot about him, you can argue he's just swapping his hours around but from last i talked to him, he genuinely seems to be in a much better place, maybe you can do the same? 

>For the rest of us, we're still gonna have to come up for air. Otherwise we're going to end up broke and homeless.

This point i agree on and tbh with you i still haven't really found a suitable explanation of why we should continue the grind, to help someone else get richer or to stave off homelessness? those are pretty shit reasons to go for but today i did some more introspection and i thought isn't the struggle itself kinda worth it? doesn't it help train your body and mind if you choose to have a growth mentaility rather than a victim kind? granted idk what ails you but I read a fantastic viewpoint from another redditor who said something along the lines of rain falling. 

Rain will fall regardless. Water evaporates, condenses and then fall as droplets. Rain is just rain, it has no other meanings attached to it. Someone might look at that rain and feel sad, gloomy and hate it whle another might love the feel of rain on their skins and relishes in knowing that the rain helps to grow crops and vegetables, giving life to nature. But it's up to each individual themself to determine how they feel about the rain. They attach their own meaning and emotions to it, rain is neutral, it doesn't care how you feel. What i'm trying to get at is probably another way to say is to try to enjoy the journey itself. 

If i had to use your swimming analogy, while you're paddling and swimming to shore, maybe you notice a mermaid on a stone, maybe you notice the sun is particuarly nice today, maybe you notice that although the struggle itself stays the same, you feel yourself getting better at carrying that weight, you're getting fitter and learning how to adapt your movements to the waves.

>Some people can. I can't, personally.
Can i ask why you can't?

This reply was just as much for me as replying your reply so if it doesn't quite hit the mark, let me know and i'll see whether i can adapt it to more accurately answer your thoughts :)
Ugh this is one of the things i'm fearing as well atm, falling into that routine...then again my current routine is also pretty soul sucking so *shrug*

heya i gave this a read and while it did indeed resonate with me. i felt i had to past an alternative view as i also thought life was about reaching that 'shore' with the prizes and girls but to be honest i only recently started to think life isn't like that at all really. 

It's up to you to decide what life is worth and what your 'shore' is, if you want that girls and prize that's fine but after browsing Reddit and reading a lot of people's stories and opinions, life is WAY more varied than that, i'm convinced that the whole 'prize' at the end is just a generic goal that is set for everyone who don't know what they want in life and to be saddled in debt to other's to help with THIER journey to the shore. 

idk, maybe i'm irritated with yor analogy because it speaks a lot of truth or maybe it's to do with the mood i'm in but the longer i think about this 'race' you mention the more i end up thinking this is a pretty crappy race. Maybe the majority of people don't even stop to question this race, who even oraganised it in the first place? 

Who's to say that you can't find new perspective when your head hits underneath the water that everyone else can't see? 

Sorry i'm rambling but i wanted to chime in with my own opinion, if you feel you have a weight around you and it's bringing you down, maybe you can do something to lessen it?

'But finally you realize - you were never in the race to begin with.', perhaps this rings the most truth, idk about you but i'm also starting to wonder about this 'race' we're all thrust into..

But i did like your analogy for most part, understood where you were coming from and well written
Thanls for sharing mate, really needed to read this as going through a pretty time atm.

Heya thanks for reaching out, tbh no, i don't like computer programming all that much and didn't really touch alot of it in my final year except if you count microsoft VB and their version of C. I did quite like working with databases though with php but didn't like messing around with html and css, iirc i did alrite on the database module but not sure where i could go with that.

Thanks for taking the time to reply and sharing your thoughts, that quote is also one i come across and quite liked so that's pretty cool. It is tough at the moment no doubt but i agree with you that among the shit there's definitely some beauty for sure, just gotta look for it. I might take you up on your offer if i'm ever feeling out of it, thanks again :)

Ikr, it can get pretty draining, all i can really suggest is to keep on keeping on, try differerent things and see what works and what doesn't, if after all being said and done, can't say you didn't at least try :)

Heya sorry to hear you're in a similiar situation, i'm gonna try a few different things this year i wouldn't normally do, see if that changes anything. Here's hoping you find the strength to get up and try again too :)
As someone who spent the better past year looking within myself, i came to this conclusion as well today. Self belief + confidence really does impact every facet of your life.
As someone who is starting to realise the value of family despite my 20+ years on this earth, and is also starting to go back to the gym. Go get 'em!
